newsitem.title: UK: Business survey puts telecoms before politics.
newsitem.headline: Business survey puts telecoms before politics.

text.p: A good telecommunications infrastructure is more vital for successful global expansion than political stability and a skilled workforce, a survey of senior corporate executives found on Thursday.

The Gallup survey of 327 of the world's largest corporations, commissioned by British Telecommunications Plc and its partner MCI, ranked telecoms well above such traditional criteria as cost of capital, cost of raw materials and transport.

Publishing the survey, attached to a BT/MCI Global Communications report, the groups said that by the year 2000, telecommunications would be worth more than $650 billion and would account for 2.37 percent of world GDP.
"It is clear that telecommunications competition encourages investment by foreign companies," said Sir Peter Bonfield, BT's chief executive.

"The UK experience has shown that competition is good for customers and good for the UK economy and we would encourage national governments to open their markets to reap the benefit of increased investment".

Gerald Taylor, the president and chief operating officer at MCI, urged business people and governments to recognise "the crucial role that competitive communications plays not only in successful global expansion, but also in the development of national economies".
"The challenge we are issuing today is to ensure that communications issues, including global deregulation, remain high on the agenda for the entire business community," he said.
An estimated 50 million people will use the Internet this year, double 1995 figures, the report added, and business and retail transactions on the net are estimated to reach $21 billion by 2000.

Telecoms traffic is also expected to surge. While the world spent nearly 60 billion minutes on the phone last year, in 2000, this could rise to 95 billion minutes, according to the report. BT/MCI Global Communications Report, 1996/97, was published in the third anniversary year of the creation by BT and MCI of their Concert alliance -- one of three alliances of global carriers.
